segments.speaker: bree_tallow
segments.text: Colder everywhere. The dockside fields froze the night you left with it. Folk are blaming the weather. I'm not.

segments.speaker: bree_tallow
segments.text: I'm not saying you were wrong. I'm saying somebody's paying for it, and it's not the ones who decided.

segments.speaker: bree_tallow
segments.text: Still there. I send them soup at midnight. One of them cried, last week. Said the glow reminds him of his mother's kitchen.

segments.speaker: bree_tallow
segments.text: Town's warmer for it. For now. Everyone knows it won't last, so nobody says so.

segments.speaker: bree_tallow
segments.text: Next to nothing, apiece. Everyone's warm and cheerful, and half of them can't remember what they had for breakfast.

segments.speaker: bree_tallow
segments.text: I won't buy one. I've lost enough to Gran's old shard. I'll not hurry the rest along.

segments.speaker: townsfolk_barmaid
segments.text: Every hearth in town has a new shard. Bree won't buy one. Says she's forgotten enough.
